blocks.text:
In the morning, set off for the north of the island with an English-speaking guide.

The first stop is Juan Griego, the island’s second most important town.

Visit La Galera Fortress, built by the Spaniards in 1810.

Next is the open-air museum Pueblo de Margarita. Each house is dedicated to the islanders’ former way of life, crafts and everyday customs.

Continue to La Asunción, the capital of Nueva Esparta state, founded in 1562.

See Simón Bolívar Square, the Church of Nuestra Señora de La Asunción and the El Valle valley.

The Basilica of Our Lady of El Valle stands here, a major pilgrimage site in Venezuela.

The next stop is San Carlos de Borromeo Fortress, built in 1622. It is in Pampatar, an area with many restaurants, cafés, art galleries and studios.

Lunch on the town beach includes traditional pescado frito fish dishes and a drink.

After lunch, walk along the bay, see the island’s main lighthouse and pink salt lakes, and enjoy views of the Los Frailes archipelago.

Return to the hotel in the evening.
